doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Leonard Feather's 1960 entry calling Gibbs the bop Lionel Hampton
summary: Rowe reads Feather's encyclopedia entry; Gibbs thinks it reflects popularity alongside Milt Jackson and says he is a bebopper.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: So I’m going to read — this is the Leonard Feather Encyclopedia of Jazz from 1960. And one Terry Gibbs, even back then, had an entry in it, and at the end it says, “Gibbs has always played with tremendous vitality and a natural beat that established him as the bop era’s equivalent of Lionel Hampton.”

Well I don’t know what he means. I don’t know what he means by that. I think maybe popularity or something, because Milt Jackson and I were the only two vibes players on the scene at the time who got well known as vibes players until Teddy Charles and Joe Roland, and another whole bunch of musicians. But we were the first two so there was Lionel Hampton and Red Norvo, so maybe — I’m not sure, but Leonard saw it like that.
I think that he wanted to make a distinction between the styles and the fact that you embraced bebop as a musical language and were able to play it on the vibes. I’m assuming that’s his point.

I am a bebop player, you know something, no matter what kind of music they want to call it I am a bebopper. And that’s the kind of music I love, that’s the kind of music I play, that’s the kind of musicians I hired to play with me but I was always playing you know.
